subject: Retained frozen inventory of failed live Preparation de491791-2e5a-45da-9ff4-2b915de42f07

verdict.statement: Applicability is a first-class, claim-authoritative source proposition (SCOPE / CONDITION), authored by Claim Discovery before the freeze. The structured actor is an addressee LABEL on the operative proposition, not applicability. The defect is that the freeze did not require authoring capability.
rejected: B (pure structured projection): not equivalent, see questions 2 and 5
C (hybrid): its second leg (projection) has no sound deterministic source in this fixture

questions.1_is_applicability_absent_from_source_in: No. The source states it, but not as applicability-bearing claims: the addressee label is in operative.actor on all 17 normative claims; triggers are embedded in the statements of a904a30b, e68ff98e, c66f0063, 11cc55af, ec585d27 and as action-embedded start/request triggers in 14b91c88 and bfe5c0e8; defined-role criteria are in 4 DEFINITION claims; time scoping is in 2 TEMPORAL_RULE claims. None of it is expressed as a SCOPE or CONDITION claim.
questions.2_is_it_present_structurally_but_lost_be: Only the addressee LABEL is structural. The domain contract (LegalRequirement.applicabilityConditions) says "a label is never its own explanation": when the source names a role and defines its criteria, those criteria must be unpacked and cited. Here the labels are defined terms (covered service, operator, fulfillment provider: DEFINITION claims 2d1a3847, 5c10d55e, 4e9e6e74, 504a4226), so projecting operative.actor would emit exactly the unexplained label the contract forbids. Triggers inside prose cannot be extracted without interpreting prose, which no validator or runtime step may do. Definitions may not be counted as applicability.
questions.3_did_claim_discovery_fail_to_emit_requi: Yes. instructions.md told the Agent to register SCOPE/CONDITION claims "if needed"; it registered none (0 of 38) although it authored 17 normative claims, 4 defined-role definitions and at least 5 conditional or triggered duties. A previous live run of the same fixture class (94773fa8) did register 2 SCOPE and 2 CONDITION claims of 35, so the omission is run-level variance in Agent output, not an impossible contract. The earlier run never reached Rule authoring, so it does not prove those claims were sufficient.
questions.4_did_the_domain_schema_encode_applicabi: No. Every Requirement field that evidence tests (applicabilityConditions, qualifiers, exceptions, semanticContext) requires claim authority by design (semantic-claim-integrity.validator.ts), so the runtime never classifies prose. The narrow point is only the gate placement: CLAIM_INVENTORY_READY did not check a condition that is NECESSARY for every valid Rule Set (see necessityProof).
questions.5_is_rule_authoring_wrongly_requiring_a_: No. The structured bindings do not provide equivalent semantics (question 2) and a projection would create a second authority path for the same field. Equivalent provenance exists only when the Agent has interpreted the source into a claim.

necessityProof: A submitted Rule Set needs packet.assessmentRules.length >= 1 (compliance-rule-set-integrity.validator.ts:105-110 EMPTY_RULE_SET).
An AssessmentRule must link an assessable LegalRequirement (coverage COVERED_BY_ASSESSMENT_RULES, INCOMPLETE_RULE_COVERAGE otherwise).

An assessable LegalRequirement needs a non-empty applicabilityConditions list (declaresApplicabilityScope, applicability.ts:143; APPLICABILITY_SCOPE_MISSING at compliance-rule-set-integrity.validator.ts:416-428).
Every applicabilityConditions[i] must equal the statement of a claim bound with role APPLICABILITY_CONDITION (semantic-claim-integrity.validator.ts:346 and :391-399 "has no claim authority").
The role matrix grants APPLICABILITY_CONDITION only to CONDITION and SCOPE claims (semantic-claim-integrity.validator.ts:35-36).

Therefore an inventory with no relevant SCOPE/CONDITION claim can never yield a valid Rule Set, whatever the Agent does after the freeze. The readiness gate rejects only inventories that are already provably unauthorable, so it cannot reject a legitimate future.

whyTheFrozenInventoryCannotSatisfyTheCon: Zero of 38 claims have type CONDITION or SCOPE, so the role matrix offers no claim for APPLICABILITY_CONDITION. Every assessable author_legal_requirement call therefore fails, independently of how the Agent fills the other role arguments. Replay proof: the ideal Agent (perfect role buckets) had 0 of 17 normative claims accepted (PREFIX_REPRODUCTION.json idealAgentInfeasibility).

disposition.beforeFix: The 38-claim inventory froze (CLAIM_INVENTORY_READY) and author_legal_requirement could produce no assessable Requirement: reproduced deterministically (PREFIX_REPRODUCTION.json; live gap and state fingerprints matched exactly).
disposition.afterFix: OPTION A: finalize_semantic_claim_inventory rejects the exact retained claims with 17 machine-readable APPLICABILITY_AUTHORITY_MISSING gaps (one per normative claim, with claim type and owning source node) and does not freeze. A scripted repaired discovery (6 source-grounded SCOPE/CONDITION claims added through the real tools) then freezes, authors 9 Requirements and 8 AssessmentRules, passes the real Rule Validator on its first attempt (44/44 claims accounted) and submits.

claims.statement: A portable copy contains all customer-created records in an interoperable machine-readable format.
A covered service stores customer-created records and offers them through a digital interface.
A fulfillment provider assists the operator in delivering portable copies.
The operator controls the covered service.
Configured export software alone does not establish fulfillment of delivery.

claims.action: implement a software export function that produces a portable copy for a requesting customer
claims.conditionsEmbeddedInStatement: for a requesting customer (action-embedded request trigger)
claims.statement: The operator of a covered service must implement a software export function that produces a portable copy for a requesting customer.

claims.action: deliver the copy within seven calendar days after receiving the request
claims.conditionsEmbeddedInStatement: after receiving the request (action-embedded start trigger)
claims.statement: The operator must deliver the copy within seven calendar days after receiving the request.

claims.action: impose commercial charges or technical obstacles intended to prevent a customer moving records
claims.statement: The operator must not impose commercial charges or technical obstacles intended to prevent a customer moving their customer-created records to another service.
The prohibition is limited to charges and obstacles intended to prevent that portability; it does not prohibit charges generally.
A compensation policy alone does not perform this payment duty.

claims.action: compensate customer for documented financial loss within thirty calendar days after receiving notice
claims.conditionsEmbeddedInStatement: If failure to perform Article 2(1) causes a customer documented financial loss
claims.statement: If failure to perform Article 2(1) causes a customer documented financial loss, the operator must compensate that customer for the documented loss within thirty calendar days after receiving notice of the loss.
As an exception to Article 2(2), the operator may temporarily block a transfer only while a documented, specific security threat makes that transfer unsafe.
This exception does not remove or delay the portable-copy duty in Article 2(1).
The block must be proportionate to that threat and end when the threat ends.
For covered services first operating on or after 1 January 2026, the duties in Article 2(1) and Article 2(2) apply immediately on first operation.
For covered services already operating before 1 January 2026, the duties in Article 2(1) and Article 2(2) become applicable on 1 July 2026 after a six-month transition.
This instrument takes effect on 1 January 2026.
Delegation does not remove the operator's own duty.

claims.action: implement the portable-copy software function and perform the same delivery duty required by Article 2(1)
claims.conditionsEmbeddedInStatement: When an operator delegates export fulfillment to an external fulfillment provider
claims.statement: When an operator delegates export fulfillment to an external fulfillment provider, that provider must implement the portable-copy software function and perform the same delivery duty required by Article 2(1), with the same seven-day period and the definitions in Article 1.
This paragraph supplies context and definitions; it creates no independent duty, prohibition or permission.
Repository storage means the storage surface used by the covered service for customer-created records.
An audit entry means the event record about an export request.

claims.action: Record authorization decision, completion or failure with timestamp in an audit entry for the export function
claims.statement: For the export function, the operator must record the authorization decision in an audit entry and must record completion or failure with its timestamp in the audit entry. These two audit duties are compatible and both must survive a combined representation.

claims.action: Implement appropriate software safeguards protecting customer-created records during processing and export
claims.statement: The operator must implement appropriate software safeguards protecting customer-created records during processing and export.

claims.action: Maintain a software configuration identifying the relevant covered service
claims.statement: The operator of a covered service must maintain a software configuration that identifies the relevant covered service.

claims.action: Record authorization decision and completion/failure with timestamp in an audit entry
claims.statement: For its export function, the operator must record the authorization decision in an audit entry and must record completion or failure with its timestamp in the audit entry. These two audit duties are compatible and both must survive a combined representation.
A repository assessment may inspect storage encryption as one narrower evidence slice; this does not replace the safeguards duty or require a particular cipher.
B performs fulfillment, but A remains responsible for export compliance.
B's duty in Article 5 does not transfer or replace A's duty.
Actor A is the covered-service operator and holder of Article 2(1). Actor B is the fulfillment provider.
B must implement the portable-copy software path for the delegated export fulfillment.

claims.action: maintain software configuration identifying B as delegate
claims.conditionsEmbeddedInStatement: If A delegates export fulfillment to B
claims.statement: If A delegates export fulfillment to B, A must maintain a software configuration identifying B as its delegate for that service.
An auditor may access records for compliance inspection.

claims.action: request access to records held by B
claims.statement: Any customer may request access to their records held by B.

claims.action: demonstrate whether the security incident condition holds and whether any restriction respects it
claims.statement: Evidence must demonstrate whether the security incident condition holds and whether any restriction respects it.
The restriction must end when the security incident condition ceases.

claims.action: restrict access to the export interface
claims.conditionsEmbeddedInStatement: only while a documented, specific security incident makes access unsafe
claims.statement: The operator may restrict access to the export interface only while a documented, specific security incident makes access unsafe.
This does not require automatic blocking, automatic unblocking, or any particular technical implementation.
